claims_observed: PortAudio can be compiled directly on Raspberry Pi
PortAudio uses ALSA on Raspberry Pi
the project documents running pa_devs and paex_sine examples on Raspberry Pi

adaptation.likely_bridge: Dart FFI or a Raspberry-Pi platform implementation behind platform.audio_io.v1

findings: test/patest_suggested_vs_streaminfo_latency.py invokes a local PATest.exe through os.system()
security.finding_context: The exact test helper constructs a local executable command to generate latency CSV data; this is not treated as harmless automatically, so the gate remains REVIEW.
security.supply_chain_reason: no supported dependency manifest was present in scanned source

strengths: The upstream project itself documents Raspberry Pi deployment rather than relying on a generic Linux inference.
Input/output, device enumeration, format conversion and full-duplex testing align closely with the platform.audio_io boundary.
ALSA is explicitly documented for Raspberry Pi.
The repository remains actively maintained even though the latest tagged stable release is older.
risks: The latest tagged stable release is v19.7.0 from 2021; current project activity is newer than the pinned stable release.
No Flutter/Raspberry-Pi adapter has been built or executed yet.
The static gate correctly keeps process execution found in test tooling under REVIEW.
Native C supply-chain analysis is not yet covered by the Researcher's manifest analyzers.
Actual device routing and latency need validation on Raspberry Pi hardware.
